title: Ethiopian Flatbread Wrap
community: Urban Ethiopia — the street food wrap
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Kita Wrap — a large fresh kita flatbread wrapped around berbere-spiced minced meat (or lentils for fasting), silsi, fresh salad, and berbere mayo. The Ethiopian street wrap — the chapati-wrap format applied to Ethiopian street food culture.
longDesc: The Ethiopian kita wrap is the modern Ethiopian street food that bridges the traditional flatbread and the contemporary wrap format — kita is used as the wrap instead of a tortilla, and the fillings are entirely Ethiopian in character.
ingredients: 4 large kita flatbreads (ETH007) — fresh and warm
200g minced beef — browned with garlic, berbere, and onion
// OR lentil filling (for fasting) — see ETH165
steps: Cook meat filling: brown mince with onion, garlic, and berbere until dry. Season.
Warm kita in a dry pan — must be warm to fold without breaking.
Add filling in a line across the centre.
Roll tightly. Wrap bottom in paper or foil.
chefTips: Warm kita is essential — cold kita cracks when folded.
Wrap tightly — filling must not escape.
cookingScience: See ETH007 for kita science. Warm kita has a more elastic gluten network than cold kita — the gluten (which becomes more rigid as it cools and partially retrogrades) is still flexible when warm, allowing the flatbread to fold without tearing.
sustainabilityTips: Kita as a wrap is more sustainable than imported tortillas.
culturalNote: The Ethiopian kita wrap is the urban food culture's adaptation — young Ethiopians who grew up with injera and Doro Wat also grew up with global food culture, and the wrap format applied to Ethiopian flavours is their natural synthesis.
